trips.description: Honeymoon. 27 nights, Tokyo → Hakone → Fuji → Matsumoto → Takayama → Kanazawa → Kyoto → Osaka → Atami → Tokyo. Ground rules for this itinerary: one timed anchor per day, never two. Start time varies with what actually opens that day, but never later than 10:00. Nothing scheduled after 20:00. Travel days count as light days, not as free days to fill.

zones.name: Hakone
zones.summary: Onsen town in the mountains — hot springs, the Hakone loop and (weather permitting) Mt. Fuji views over Lake Ashi.

zones.name: Fujikawaguchiko
zones.summary: Lake Kawaguchi at the foot of Mt. Fuji — the classic postcard views.

zones.name: Matsumoto
zones.summary: Castle town in the Japanese Alps — one-night stop between Fuji and Takayama.

zones.name: Takayama
zones.summary: Beautifully preserved old town in the Hida mountains — morning markets and Hida beef.

zones.name: Kanazawa
zones.summary: Edo-period districts, one of Japan's top three gardens, and a great food market.

zones.name: Kyoto
zones.summary: Temples, gardens, geisha districts and old streets — four full days.

zones.name: Osaka
zones.summary: Japan's kitchen — neon, street food and day-trip base (Nara, Kobe, Himeji).

zones.name: Tokyo
zones.summary: Arrival city and grand finale — Shinjuku, Shibuya, Asakusa and everything in between.

zones.name: Atami
zones.summary: Seaside onsen town on the Izu peninsula — ocean-view hot springs, kaiseki dinners and a slow wind-down before the Tokyo finale.

activities.name: BAMBOO GROVE
activities.description:
Bamboo forest walk — combine with Tenryu-ji temple and the monkey park. Go before 08:30.

Empty before 9:00, and that changes everything.

Saved as "Arashiyama Bamboo Grove"

activities.name: Atami Sun Beach and the Atami Ginza arcade
activities.name_ja: 熱海サンビーチ・熱海銀座
activities.description:
Palm-lined beach and the old shopping street right in town — easy on foot from the ryokan, good for a sunset wander in yukata.

Saved as "Atami Sun Beach & Ginza shotengai"

activities.name: CHUREITO
activities.description:
THE Fuji photo spot — pagoda + Fuji in one frame. ~400 steps up; 20 min by train from Kawaguchiko.

~400 steps, the Fuji-with-pagoda shot.

Saved as "Chureito Pagoda"

activities.name: DOTONBORI at night
activities.description:
Neon canal walk, Glico sign photo — 5 minutes from the hotel.

The Glico sign, the canal, the giant crab.

activities.name: Fushimi Inari
activities.description:
The thousand vermillion torii gates. Open 24h — sunrise or after 17:00 beats the crowds; full loop ~2h.

Climb 20 minutes and the crowd disappears.

Saved as "Fushimi Inari Shrine"

activities.name: Afternoon: Hakone Open-Air Museum
activities.description:
Sculptures in the mountains, Picasso pavilion, and a foot bath.

Sculptures and the Picasso gallery, about 2 hours. The best thing in Hakone.

Saved as "Hakone Open-Air Museum"

activities.name: Afternoon: Higashi Chaya in the late light
activities.description:
Geisha teahouse district — gold-leaf everything, including gold-leaf ice cream.

Saved as "Higashi Chaya District"

activities.name: Jogasaki Coastal Cliff Walk
activities.description: Dramatic volcanic coastline on the Izukyu line, with a suspension bridge over the cliffs. One of three options for the Izu day (with MOA Museum and Shuzenji Onsen). Pick one.

activities.name: Lake Kawaguchi
activities.description: Lakeside walk and the Panoramic Ropeway; best Fuji reflections early morning.

activities.name: Kenrokuen at opening
activities.description:
One of Japan's three great gardens — go right at opening for near-empty paths. Kanazawa Castle is next door.

One of Japan's three great gardens. The castle is next door.

Saved as "Kenroku-en Garden"

activities.name: Kinkaku-ji and the dry garden at Ryoan-ji
activities.description:
The gold-leaf pavilion over its mirror pond. 30–45 min visit; pairs well with Ryoan-ji rock garden nearby.

Saved as "Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)"

activities.name: Kiunkaku
activities.description:
A 1919 seaside villa turned ryokan, now open to the public — gorgeous gardens and a coffee salon. A calm morning stop on the Izu day.

1919 villa, beautiful gardens, café room.

activities.name: MATSUMOTO CASTLE
activities.description:
One of Japan's most beautiful original castles — the black 'Crow Castle'. Evening light-up is lovely.

Last entry 16:30. Steep stairs — clean socks.

activities.name: Pick one
activities.description:
Hilltop museum with sweeping sea views over Atami — one of three options for the Izu day (with the Jogasaki cliff walk and Shuzenji Onsen). Pick one.

MOA Museum (up the hill, sea views) / Jogasaki cliffs / Shuzenji Onsen and its bamboo forest.

Saved as "MOA Museum of Art"

activities.name: If you have energy
activities.description:
The castle park is the highlight — nice at golden hour; museum inside is skippable if short on time.

Osaka Castle and its park, Himeji (1 h, the finest castle in Japan) or Kobe.

Saved as "Osaka Castle"

activities.name: Morning: funicular Gora → Sounzan, ropeway to Owakudani
activities.description:
Volcanic valley on the Hakone ropeway — sulfur vents and the famous black eggs.

The black egg.

Saved as "Owakudani"

activities.name: Takayama Jinya, the old town, a tasting at a sake brewery
activities.description:
Preserved Edo-period streets — sake breweries, craft shops. Combine with the Miyagawa morning market by the river.

Saved as "Sanmachi Suji old town"

activities.name: Sensoji
activities.description:
Tokyo's oldest temple, in Asakusa. Before 09:00 beats the crowds on Nakamise street.

Kaminarimon → Nakamise → main hall → Asakusa Shrine.

Saved as "Senso-ji Temple"

activities.name: SHIBUYA SKY
activities.description:
The scramble crossing at dusk; Shibuya Sky observation deck needs advance tickets.

Booked entry is ~16:00 and mid-October sunset is around 17:05 — be up top before the light goes.

Saved as "Shibuya Crossing & Sky"

activities.name: Shuzenji Onsen
activities.description: Bamboo forest walk and a 1,200-year-old temple in one of Izu's oldest onsen towns. One of three options for the Izu day (with MOA Museum and the Jogasaki cliff walk). Pick one.

activities.name: teamLab PLANETS
activities.name_ja: チームラボプラネッツ
activities.description:
Immersive digital art in Toyosu. Book ~2 weeks ahead; you walk barefoot through water — wear shorts.

Out around 20:00.

activities.name: teamLab BIOVORTEX
activities.name_ja: チームラボバイオヴォルテックス京都
activities.description:
Booked: Mon 6 Oct, 09:30. Japan's largest digital art museum — 10,000 m² over four floors, 50+ works, maze-like. Budget 4 hours, not 2, and go down to the basement on entry to hit the smaller rooms first. No café inside, so eat before. Free lockers, no bags over 50 cm. Sneakers (there's an athletics area), plain light clothing for photos, no short skirts because of the mirrored floors.

Budget 4 hours, not 2. On entry, go down to the basement and hit the smaller rooms first.

Saved as "teamLab Biovortex Kyoto"
activities.address: 21-5 Higashikujo Higashi-Iwamotocho, Minami-ku, Kyoto — 7 min on foot from the Hachijo East exit of Kyoto Station

activities.name: Universal Studios Japan
activities.name_ja: ユニバーサル・スタジオ・ジャパン
activities.description: Oct 8 — our full USJ day (Halloween season + the park's 25th anniversary). Tickets go on sale ~2 months ahead — expect Aug 8–14, 2026 — and you must buy the day they open: there are NO ticket booths at the park anymore (online only, via Klook). Get 2× Studio Pass + 2× Universal Express Pass Premium for Oct 8. The day-by-day plan is in the schedule; the complete guide we made is attached below.

activities.name: Kaiseki at the ryokan
activities.description:
The local specialties — kinmedai (golden eye snapper) and ise-ebi spiny lobster, in season from October. Fresh Izu wasabi and sakura-ebi (cherry blossom shrimp) from Suruga Bay too. Best had as the ryokan's kaiseki dinner.

Kinmedai, and ise-ebi — the lobster that comes into season right in October.

Saved as "Kinmedai & ise-ebi kaiseki"

activities.name: Matcha stop in Gion
activities.description: Placeholder pick — matcha parfait/tea house in Gion; expect queues after 11:00.

activities.name: Okonomiyaki & takoyaki crawl
activities.description: Placeholder pick — okonomiyaki dinner around Dotonbori/Namba, takoyaki stands for dessert.

activities.name: Ramen night in Shinjuku
activities.description: Placeholder pick — Omoide Yokocho alleys are next to the hotel; ticket machines, cash only.

activities.name: Atami Sekaie
activities.description: Oct 10 – 12 · Atami · Booking.com, confirmed, ₪6,768. Premium ocean-view ryokan — the pick for the Izu stop. A backup booking at Yuyado Ichibanchi (₪3,750, same dates) is still open — cancel it when you get a chance, both are free to cancel.

activities.name: Candeo Hotels Osaka Shinsaibashi
activities.name_ja: カンデオホテルズ大阪心斎橋
activities.description: Oct 7 – 10 · Osaka · Booking.com, confirmed, ₪2,056. Excellent Shinsaibashi location, steps from Dotonbori. Candeo's signature is a top-floor sky spa — check whether it's included. In-room washing machine, good for a laundry night.

activities.name: Hotel Gracery Shinjuku
activities.name_ja: ホテルグレイスリー新宿
activities.description: Sep 19 – 25 & Oct 12 – 16 · Tokyo (Shinjuku) · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪3,233. The Godzilla-head hotel in Kabukicho — covers both the arrival leg and the final leg. Ask for a high floor away from the street; Kabukicho is loud until 3–4am.

activities.name: Hakone Yutowa
activities.description: Sep 25 – 27 · Hakone · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪1,920. Modern ryokan in Gora. Booking.com is offering an upgrade to a superior room WITH PRIVATE BATH, which implies the booked room may not have one — check and consider upgrading.

activities.name: Mitsui Garden Hotel Kyoto Shinmachi Bettei
activities.name_ja: 三井ガーデンホテル京都新町別邸
activities.description: Oct 3 – 7 · Kyoto · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪2,531. Machiya-style hotel on Shinmachi street, CENTRAL Kyoto — great for Nishiki, Gion and Pontocho, but a metro ride (not a 7-min walk) from teamLab Biovortex near the station.

activities.name: Mizno Hotel
activities.description: Sep 27 – 28 · Fujikawaguchiko · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪810. One night before the Chureito sunrise. Upgrade offered to a superior room with balcony (lake/Fuji view). Confirm parking (you'll have the rental car) and ask about a very early checkout for the sunrise start.

activities.name: Onyado Nono Matsumoto Natural Hot Spring
activities.description: Sep 28 – 29 · Matsumoto · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪470. Natural hot spring baths, tatami-style, excellent value. Arrange takkyubin (luggage forwarding) here — bags go ahead to Takayama since you can't bring them into Kamikochi.

activities.name: The HOTEL SANRAKU KANAZAWA
activities.description: Oct 1 – 3 · Kanazawa · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪1,664. Return the rental car THE DAY YOU ARRIVE (Oct 1), not the next day — Kanazawa is entirely walkable and parking costs money. Refuel before drop-off.

activities.name: HOTEL WOOD TAKAYAMA
activities.description: Sep 29 – Oct 1 · Takayama · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪935. You arrive here tired after the Kamikochi traverse. Confirm parking and whether dinner is included — you'll want it after that day.

activities.name: Land at Narita
activities.description: Scan your Visit Japan Web QR at the Joint Kiosk. Between immigration, bags and customs you'll be out around 20:30–21:00.

activities.name: Narita Express or Limousine Bus into the city
activities.description: 60–90 min. Buy the ticket before you head down to the platform.

activities.name: At the hotel
activities.description: Stop at a konbini for water, breakfast and something to snack on. Then sleep.

activities.name: Have the QR ready and your phone charged

activities.name: Meiji Jingu and Yoyogi Park
activities.description: Calm mid-morning.

activities.name: Takeshita Street

activities.name: Lunch — Afuri Harajuku
activities.description: Yuzu-shio ramen.

activities.name: THE HEAD SPA SHIBUYA (90 min)

activities.name: SUSHI KENSHIN — birthday dinner
activities.description: Tell the restaurant it's a birthday when you book.

activities.name: Sneakers: measure your foot in cm before you fly
activities.description: Japanese sizing is foot length. If you have wide feet, ask for Japanese Asics or Mizuno models in 2E or 4E width. Bring the socks you'll actually walk in. Backup if nothing fits: Alpen Tokyo, Shinjuku. And don't break in new shoes the next day — bring a comfortable pair from home and rotate the new ones in a few hours at a time.

activities.name: TSUKIJI
activities.description: Graze, don't fill up.

activities.name: Hama Rikyu, the garden next door
Back to the hotel. Long nap

activities.name: MAGURO MART
activities.description: The tuna set, and the nakaochi you scrape yourself.

activities.name: Tsukiji is the outer market, not the wholesale one
activities.description: The auction moved to Toyosu in 2018. Before 10:00 or it isn't worth it. Graze in small bites: tamagoyaki, uni, a grilled scallop, strawberry daifuku. Bring cash and a small bag for rubbish — there are no bins.

activities.name: Nishi-Sando
activities.description: Kagetsudo melonpan — before 14:00, it sells out.

activities.name: Suzukien

activities.name: Sumida Park
activities.description: Skytree across the river.

activities.name: ANN FRAGRANCE Asakusa
activities.description: Custom perfume, ~50 min.

activities.name: Kappabashi

activities.name: Akihabara
activities.description: Yodobashi, Super Potato, gachapon.

activities.name: Kappabashi closes at 17:00
activities.description: Drop your purchases in a coin locker at Akihabara Station (¥400–700) and walk around unloaded. If you buy something heavy, several shops will send it to the hotel by takkyubin. No kimono in Tokyo — you do it once, in Kyoto on 5/10.

activities.name: Tourist discount card at the department store counter
activities.description: This first.

activities.name: Mikimoto, Itoya
activities.description: 12 floors of stationery.

activities.name: OMAKASE
activities.description: Lunch is far better value than dinner.

activities.name: Feiler flagship

activities.description: ~25 min.

activities.name: Dinner in Toyosu on the way out
activities.description: Or something light back in Shinjuku.

activities.name: Leave Ginza empty-handed
activities.description: Ginza and Toyosu are directly connected by the Yurikamome — no need to go back to the hotel in between. You walk through water at teamLab and the lockers are free, but you don't want to carry bags all day; if you buy anything bulky, have it sent to the hotel. Clothes you can roll up to the knee, no long skirts (mirrored floors), shoes that come off easily.

activities.name: Isetan
activities.description: Discount card first.

activities.name: JINS
activities.description: Glasses, ready in ~30 min.

activities.name: Evening: pack without rushing
activities.description: Takkyubin to Hakone if you want to travel light.

activities.name: Don't buy consumables tax-free yet
activities.description: They get sealed and you can't open them until you leave Japan. That's 13/10.

activities.name: Shinkansen Tokyo → Odawara, then on to Gora

activities.name: Midday: ropeway to Togendai, pirate ship across Lake Ashi to Motohakone
Afternoon: Hakone Shrine's floating torii
activities.description: Bus back to Gora.

activities.name: Fuji shows itself best in the morning

activities.name: Down to Odawara and pick up the car

activities.name: Gotemba Premium Outlets
activities.description: Tourist coupon at the info desk — bring your passport.

activities.name: Drive to Kawaguchiko (1 h). Check in
Oishi Park

activities.name: Evening: houtou
activities.description: Thick noodles in miso broth.

activities.name: Oshino Hakkai
activities.description: Eight snowmelt ponds, thatched roofs, spring-water tofu.

activities.name: Drive to Matsumoto
activities.description: 2–2:30 via the Chuo Expressway.

activities.name: Evening: Nawate-dori and Nakamachi
activities.description: Matsumoto soba, local sake.

activities.name: A 7:00 start is what makes both Chureito and Oshino fit

activities.name: Route 158 → Abo Tunnel → AKANDANA car park
activities.description: ¥600. Direct shuttle in from there.

activities.name: KAMIKOCHI, 1,500 m
activities.description: Flat riverside walk: Taisho Pond (morning mist is the shot) → Kappa Bridge → Myojin Pond. 3–4 hours, no climbing.

activities.name: Shuttle back, collect the car, drive to Takayama
Evening: the ryokan
activities.description: Yukata, onsen, kaiseki dinner.

activities.name: Private cars are banned in Kamikochi
activities.description: Akandana rather than Sawando because it's on the Takayama side: you end the day an hour from the ryokan. Free foot onsen at the Hirayu terminal. There are no bins — you carry everything out. Eat at one of the Kamikochi lodges; there's nothing between stops.

activities.name: Miyagawa Market along the river
activities.description: Closes at 12:00.

activities.name: Afternoon: Hida Folk Village (optional)
activities.description: Or the old town again, without rushing.

activities.name: Food: Hida beef
activities.description: Hida beef nigiri on a rice cracker. Grilled Hida beef in the evening.

activities.name: Worth buying: sarubobo dolls, sake, woodcraft
SHIRAKAWA-GO
activities.description: 50 min from Takayama. Shiroyama viewpoint, Wada House, the rice paddies.

activities.name: Refuel before handing it back
activities.description: Or they charge a punitive rate. Out-of-prefecture returns usually have to land inside business hours (until ~20:00) — leave margin. Check the one-way drop-off fee is included in what you were quoted.

activities.name: Nagamachi samurai district
activities.description: 21st Century Museum next — the swimming pool illusion.

activities.name: Afternoon: back to Higashi Chaya
activities.description: Gold-leaf ice cream. A gold-leaf workshop if you fancy it.

activities.name: Hokuriku Shinkansen Kanazawa → Tsuruga, change to the Thunderbird → Kyoto
activities.description: ~2 h all in.

activities.name: Wander the neighbourhood with no plan
activities.description: Nishiki in passing, a coffee, the Kamo River.

activities.name: Pontocho by the river
activities.description: First dinner in Kyoto.

activities.name: Togetsukyo Bridge, riverside walk
activities.description: % Arabica.

activities.name: Back to the centre
activities.description: Evening free.

activities.name: KIMONO
activities.description: The only one of the trip.

activities.name: Kiyomizudera → Sanneizaka → Ninenzaka → Yasaka Pagoda → Gion Hanamikoji
activities.description: This is the sunset walk, and it's the whole point of the day.

activities.name: ENEN
activities.description: Grilled wagyu — order less than you think.

activities.name: Ask the kimono shop for an 18:00 return
activities.description: Or a next-morning return, which several shops offer. A 17:30 return means you miss the sunset, which is the whole point of the day.

activities.name: Head out
activities.description: Eat before — there's no café inside.

activities.name: Free afternoon
activities.description: Philosopher's Path, Ginkaku-ji, a tea ceremony, or nothing.

activities.name: Kyoto farewell dinner
activities.description: Pontocho or Gion.

activities.name: This is not a two-hour visit
activities.description: 10,000 m² over four floors, 50+ works, maze-like: 3 hours is the sensible minimum and 4–5 if it's your first teamLab. 7 minutes on foot from the Hachijo East exit of Kyoto Station. Free lockers, no bags over 50 cm. Sneakers (there's an athletics area), plain light clothing for photos, no short skirts because of the mirrored floors.

activities.name: Kintetsu Limited Express, Kyoto → Nara
activities.description: ~45 min.

activities.name: Luggage into the lockers at Kintetsu Nara Station
Nara Park
activities.description: Bow to the deer and they bow back.

activities.name: Todai-ji and the Great Buddha
activities.description: Year 728.

activities.name: Lunch in Naramachi
activities.description: Kasuga Taisha and its lantern paths if you still have legs.

activities.name: Collect the luggage. Kintetsu Nara → Osaka Namba
activities.description: ~40 min.

activities.name: Check in at Candeo Shinsaibashi
activities.description: Ask for a high floor.

activities.name: Late: Noguchi Taro Ramen Shinsaibashi
activities.description: 17:00–04:00, no sign on the door, 5 min from the hotel.

activities.name: Kyoto → Nara → Osaka is all one Kintetsu line
activities.description: No crossing the city, no changing operators. Namba drops you steps from the hotel. Luggage: simplest is the large lockers at Kintetsu Nara Station (~¥700). The alternative is takkyubin from the Kyoto hotel on the morning of the 6th — it reaches Osaka on the 7th — but then you need an overnight bag for the night of the 6th. There's a washing machine in the Osaka room; use it.

activities.name: Kuromon Market before midday
activities.description: Wagyu skewers, uni, scallops, fruit.

activities.name: Tennoji Park → Shinsekai
activities.description: Tsutenkaku and the kushikatsu alleys.

activities.name: Umeda Sky Building at sunset
activities.description: The open ring on the roof.

activities.name: If you're tired, sleep in
activities.description: Walk around the neighbourhood — that's allowed. That's what the day is for.

activities.name: If not
activities.description: Sumiyoshi Taisha, the Kaiyukan aquarium, or nothing.

activities.name: Buy 551 Horai pork buns for tomorrow's train
TAKKYUBIN: big suitcases straight to the Tokyo hotel
activities.description: They'll be waiting at the Gracery when you get back on the 12th.

activities.description: 2:15, change at Shin-Yokohama or Odawara.

activities.name: Check in at the ryokan. Yukata
Back to the ryokan
activities.description: Long onsen. Second kaiseki. Nothing scheduled.

activities.name: Izu gets Pacific typhoons into October
activities.description: If the forecast turns, stay close to Atami — Shimoda can get cut off.

activities.name: Shinkansen Atami → Tokyo

activities.name: Check in at the Gracery, Kabukicho
activities.description: Ask for a high floor away from the street — the area is loud until 3 or 4.

activities.name: Evening: Omoide Yokocho, yakitori in the alleys

activities.name: Coffee first
activities.description: Shops open 10:00–11:00.

activities.name: Bic Camera
activities.description: The ReFa. If you buy a hair dryer, insist on a 100–240V model — 100V ones burn out at home. Open the Bic Camera coupon on your phone before choosing.

activities.name: Drugstore

activities.description: They're sealed and you can't open them until you leave Japan. Stack the discounts: tax-free (min. ¥5,000) + Bic Camera coupon (5–7%) + Donki coupon + department store tourist card (~5%). Always confirm before the register. If the 13th is grey, move Shibuya Sky to the 14th — you have the day free.

activities.name: Yokohama
activities.description: Chinatown, Cup Noodle Museum, Red Brick Warehouse. 30 min away.

activities.name: Hidden Tokyo
activities.description: Yanaka and its pre-war lanes, vintage Shimokitazawa, Kagurazaka.

activities.name: Nothing
activities.description: It's day 26 of 27.

activities.name: This is the Shibuya Sky backup
activities.description: If the 13th was grey, today is the spare slot.

activities.name: Sleep in. Last konbini breakfast

Pack

tips.body: Hakone Free Pass covers the whole loop (train, cable car, ropeway, pirate boat) and discounts many sights.
Use luggage forwarding (takkyubin) to send big bags ahead to a later hotel — travel the Fuji–Alps stretch light.
Fuji hides in clouds by late morning — plan viewpoints for early morning and check a Fuji visibility forecast.
Everything is walkable: station → Nakamachi street → castle in 20 minutes.
Hida beef is the local specialty — beef sushi at the market stalls, or a proper grill dinner.
The Kanazawa Loop Bus connects all the sights; day pass pays off with 3+ rides.
Buses get packed — prefer subway + walking; taxis are reasonable for 2 people on short hops.
Stand on the RIGHT on escalators in Osaka (opposite of Tokyo).
Get a Suica/Pasmo in Apple/Google Wallet for all trains, metro and convenience stores.
Trash cans are rare — carry a small bag for garbage.
Onsen etiquette: wash sitting down before entering the bath; towels stay out of the water.
Ask for a high floor on the Godzilla side; the head 'roars' on schedule from the 8F terrace.
Open 24h — sunrise or after 17:00 for photos without crowds.
Izu absorbs Pacific storms through October. If the forecast turns, stay north near Atami — Shimoda can get cut off.
Choose a room with a private open-air bath facing the sea if the budget allows — this is the trip's wind-down stretch.
Cancel the backup Yuyado Ichibanchi booking (Oct 10–12) when you get a chance — Atami Sekaie is the one you're keeping.

shopping.name: Onitsuka Tiger Mexico 66
shopping.note: The classic sneakers — much cheaper here than at home. Try them on: Japanese sizing runs narrow.
shopping.shop: Onitsuka Tiger store or ABC Mart

shopping.name: Uniqlo HEATTECH base layers
shopping.note: The Japan-only range is wider and cheaper. Size up — an L at home is often XL/2XL here.
shopping.shop: Uniqlo (Ginza flagship is the big one)

shopping.name: Uniqlo UT collab tees
shopping.note: Japan-exclusive prints you cannot get at home. Good, light souvenirs.

shopping.name: Ichikami / Tsubaki shampoo + conditioner
shopping.note: The famous Japanese hair care. Cheapest at Donki or a drugstore, not the airport.

shopping.name: Shiseido Fino hair mask
shopping.note: Tiny tub, cult status, costs a fraction of the export price.

shopping.name: Throat spray + hot-eye masks
shopping.note: The konbini throat spray the group swore by, and the Kao steam eye masks.

shopping.name: Regional Kit Kat flavours
shopping.note: Matcha in Kyoto, wasabi near Fuji — buy them where they are local.

shopping.name: Kitchen knife
shopping.note: Buy it in Kyoto or Osaka where the knife shops are, and get it wrapped for hold luggage.

shopping.name: Stationery haul (pens, notebooks)
shopping.note: Uni-ball, Pilot, Midori notebooks — a whole floor of them at Loft or Itoya.

shopping.name: Donki souvenir run
shopping.note: The one-stop shop for cheap gifts. Bring your passport for tax-free over ¥5,000.
